evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription of Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai’s Qing commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen entry says 箇 is a bamboo measure/stalk (竹枚) and is made from 竹 with 固 as phonetic. Duan’s commentary says the text also has 个 as an alternative form meaning half a bamboo; he attributes this report to a Tang edition quoted in 六書故 and discusses later uses of 个 for an individual piece. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of every proposed graphic or semantic link.
evidence.title: 說文解字「箇」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 個 variant entry A00190-001 and A00190-002
evidence.text: The entry says Shuowen has no 個 headword, quotes the 箇/个 account, and reports 儀禮·士虞禮 with three 个 and Zheng Xuan’s gloss equating 个 with 枚 and noting the vernacular name 個. It classifies 个 as a variant of 個 in its modern variant inventory. For 亇, it cites Song-Yuan俗字譜 material and describes a graphic alteration from another variant. Its listed ancient inscriptional reference fields for 个 are unavailable, so this source does not establish an oracle-bone or bronze ancestry.
evidence.title: [A00190] 個 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Hanyu Da Cidian/ZDIC transcription of Kangxi and Shuowen entries
evidence.field: 个: Kangxi; cross-reference to 箇 in Shuowen
evidence.text: The entry records several historically distinct senses under 个: classifier glossed 枚, a personal counter, measurements in cited ritual texts, a side chamber sense, and a bamboo-branch interpretation attributed to 六書本義. It cross-references Shuowen’s 箇 entry (竹枚也，从竹固聲) and Duan’s note about 个. These are dictionary-organized attestations and inherited explanations; their sequence alone should not be treated as semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 个 gè、gě、gàn - 汉典

evidence.source: Hanyu Da Cidian/ZDIC, quoting 儀禮 and 史記 material
evidence.text: This entry cites 儀禮·士虞禮「俎釋三个」 and 史記·貨殖列傳 commentary「竹竿万个」. The first shows 个 used in a ritual counting context; the second is specifically associated by its commentary with bamboo. The quoted dictionary page does not date the composition or establish that the second use directly developed into the modern unrestricted classifier.
evidence.title: 个 gè、gě、gàn - 汉典

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, 個 entry
evidence.text: The entry maps traditional 個 to simplified 个; gives 個 the Guangyun fanqie 古賀 and the Guangyun category 見母、歌/箇韻、去聲、開口一等; and analyzes 個 as semantic 人 plus phonetic 固. It cites Zheng Xuan’s explanation at 儀禮·士虞禮 that 个 is like 枚 and the vernacular 个/個 name is similar in sound. It also lists modern single/individual senses. The entry supports the traditional phonosemantic analysis of 個, but does not make 个 itself a person-plus-固 compound.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「個」

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction table, version 1.1 (2014)
evidence.field: pronunciation comparison: 箇, 個, 个; methodology note
evidence.text: The table lists 箇, 個, and 个 with Mandarin gè, Middle Chinese kaH, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kˤa[r]-s, glossed piece/item or tally/piece/item. It explains that the Middle Chinese notation represents information from rhyme-book sources and is not itself a reconstruction. In this same system the three listed graph entries have matching readings, which supports phonetic compatibility of the written forms. It does not establish the original spoken name of bamboo or prove a historical loan from an independently recoverable bamboo-object name.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyMandarinMC2014-09-20

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 固 entry (reconstruction data attributed there to Zhengzhang 2003 and Baxter–Sagart 2014)
evidence.text: The entry gives 固 Mandarin gù, Middle Chinese Baxter kuH, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[k]ˤa-s, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *kaːs. It lists 箇 and 個 in 固’s phonetic series under Zhengzhang with *kaːls. Comparison within Baxter–Sagart therefore gives 固 *[k]ˤa-s versus 箇/個/个 *kˤa[r]-s: related but not identical reconstructed forms, consistent with a phonetic relationship rather than a claim of exact identity. Modern readings also differ in tone: 固 gù versus 個/个 gè.
evidence.title: 固 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wang Tongwei, journal abstract in 陕西理工大学学报（社会科学版）
evidence.field: abstract on historical spellings and classifier use
evidence.text: The 2017 abstract proposes that before Wei-Jin, the classifier was often written 个 and mainly counted bamboo-related objects such as arrows; from Han, 箇 became more frequent while bamboo remained a common object; during Wei-Jin through Sui, 个 often denoted side chambers and 箇 remained common as a classifier; by Tang, the numeral + 箇 + noun construction and wide-ranging classifier use were established, with 個 increasingly mixed with 箇. This is a scholar’s proposed account, available here only as an abstract; it complicates a simple bamboo-stalk > general classifier narrative and needs verification against the article’s cited corpus examples.
evidence.title: 量词“个”及其字形“个、箇、個”的历时演变

evidence.source: Hanyu Da Cidian/ZDIC, quoting Kangxi and Shuowen
evidence.text: The page reports the modern Mandarin reading gè for the classifier; its displayed cross-language data include Cantonese go3, Japanese on readings ka/ko and kun reading ko-hi, Korean kay/ka, and Vietnamese cá. It also gives Middle Chinese 見母、箇韻、去聲 and historical fanqie 古賀. The cross-language readings show present or dictionary-recorded readings, not the character’s origin or a dated sound history for each language.
evidence.title: 个 gè、gě、gàn - 汉典

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.text: The dictionary gives 個 the standard Mandarin reading gè and records classifier use for counting individual people or objects, adjectival ‘single/individual’, demonstrative this/that, and a verbal particle function. This verifies modern senses only; it does not date the semantic transitions among them.
evidence.title: 個 : (一) ㄍㄜˋ - Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary

evidence.field: scope of the cited reconstruction system
evidence.text: The authors specify that their table is a Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction list (version 1.1, 2014), sorted using Mandarin and Middle Chinese information, and that the symbols mark uncertainty where evidence does not decide presence or identity. The reported form comparison above is system-specific and must not be conflated with Zhengzhang’s *kaːls notation.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyMandarinMC2014-09-20

Duan Yucai’s commentary reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo, citing a Tang edition as quoted in 六書故. This records a historical lexicographic explanation; it does not independently establish a dated graphic chain from that form to modern 个.

evidence.text: The entry catalogs 个 as a variant of 個 and reproduces form records including a Shuowen image. Its listed oracle-bone, bronze, and several other ancient-form reference fields are marked unavailable for this entry. This supports the gap in a securely sourced early graphic chronology; it does not show that no earlier form ever existed.
evidence.title: [A00190] 個 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Hanyu Da Cidian/ZDIC transcription of Kangxi and Shuowen entries
evidence.field: 个: historical senses and cited texts
evidence.text: The entry cites 儀禮·士虞禮「俎釋三个」 and explains that Zheng Xuan glossed 个 as 枚, adding that the vernacular name 個 sounded similar. It also cites 史記·貨殖列傳「竹竿万个」 with a commentary associating 个 with bamboo. These are separate counting contexts reported through a dictionary; they do not establish the composition dates of the cited works, the earliest written attestations, or a continuous semantic development to the modern general classifier. The same entry records other senses, including side chambers and a graphic association with 介, which should not be collapsed into one origin without further evidence.

evidence.text: The entry analyzes traditional 個 as semantic 人 plus phonetic 固, and reports the 儀禮·士虞禮 passage and Zheng Xuan’s gloss that 个 is like 枚 and the vernacular name 個 is similar in sound. This supports the conventional component analysis for 個, not a claim that simplified 个 itself contains 人 and 固.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「個」

evidence.text: The table lists 箇 with Mandarin gè, Middle Chinese kaH, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kˤa[r]-s, glossed ‘piece, item’. This is one reconstruction system’s entry for 箇; it is not evidence for the original spoken name of a bamboo object or, by itself, proof of a whole-graph loan.

gaps: No character-specific oracle-bone or bronze specimen was inspected. The official variant dictionary lists its relevant inscriptional-reference fields as unavailable, so no early graphic chronology for 个 can be asserted here.

The traditional Shuowen/Duan account treats 箇 as bamboo measure/stalk and 个 as a half-bamboo variant, but the exact graphic derivation between bamboo forms and the reduced modern character has not been independently established from inspected dated specimens.

The claim that classifier use developed smoothly from ‘bamboo stalk’ to ‘piece’ to a general classifier is disputed/underspecified. A 2017 abstract proposes variant-specific and period-specific uses, while the dictionary glosses and isolated classical examples do not prove each semantic bridge.

No independently recoverable pronunciation/name for an original bamboo object was established. The phonetic compatibility of 固 and 箇/個 in historical reconstruction does not alone prove a whole-graph loan based on the object’s name.

The phonetic role 固 in traditional 個 is supported by Shuowen, the CUHK character analysis, and reconstructed comparisons; this does not make the reduced graph 个 a phonosemantic compound in its own right.
No dated corpus sequence was retrieved that establishes first attestations and exact chronology for each separate sense of 个, 箇, and 個, including demonstrative, particle, or possessive uses.
The Ctext pages returned 403 errors, and the Academia Sinica portal was consulted only through its guide; no glyph images were viewed.

No character-specific oracle-bone, bronze, or Sinica form record was inspected for 个. The MOE variant entry marks relevant ancient inscriptional-reference fields unavailable, so an oracle-bone or bronze ancestry cannot be asserted from this research.

The Shuowen/Duan account presents 箇 as bamboo-related and reports 个 as an alternate half-bamboo form, but this inherited account is not independently verified here with dated specimens. It does not establish a complete graphic pathway to modern 个.

The classical citations indicate different counting contexts, but this research did not retrieve a dated corpus sequence establishing first attestations or the semantic bridges from bamboo-related counting to the unrestricted classifier. Dictionary gloss order is not a chronology.

The etymology of the spoken source word and an independently recoverable pronunciation for a bamboo object were not established. Phonetic compatibility does not prove a whole-graph borrowing based on the object’s name.

The traditional phonetic analysis concerns 固 within 箇 or 個 as asserted by the relevant sources. Current research did not freshly establish a same-system reconstruction comparison for 固 alongside 箇, and the reduced graph 个 is not thereby shown to be a phonosemantic compound.
Modern Mandarin gè and Guangyun fanqie 古賀 are recorded in the inspected dictionary sources; no dated sound history across languages was established here.
A Commons image candidate was identified from its description, but the Commons file page open failed with a cache miss. No actual pixels were inspected in this research stage.
